results.evidence: Retry found no new figure for this Watson Lakes line. One trip report via Anderson Lakes to the East Peak gives 2,500 ft gained and lost over 6 mi; an overnight via the Watson Lakes camp gives ~3,000 ft for the scramble; WTA gives only the lakes hike (1,100 ft). The figures describe different lines and do not agree; a GPS track of this exact Watson-Lakes/east-gully line would settle it.

Sources still split: ~6 mi round trip (3 mi one way, matching dist_km 4.8 km) for the Anderson Lakes/direct line, ~8 mi round trip for the Watson Lakes overnight line, and a 2023 day trip to the tarns below the Watson Glacier clocked a little over 7 mi. None supports the 4.7-mi summit waypoint or ~9-10 mi itinerary total. A measured track of the Watson Lakes/east-gully line would settle it.

results.correct_value: The standard line climbs a steep snow finger that is a tongue of the small Watson Glacier remnant to the col between the summits; it is not glacier-free.
results.evidence: A 2020 high-route report describes carrying crampons and ice axe 'up to the little glacier, climbing a steep snow finger between the two summits'. A separate route description aims for 'the glacier finger' below the East summit and makes a rising traverse from the base of the glacier remnants to the ~5,900 ft col. An overnight report and a ski report both describe moats at the gullies/col. So the safety fields' 'no glacier travel' / 'non-glaciated' are wrong; beta, rack and obj_haz are right.

patches.value: Small glacier remnant only: the steep snow finger to the col between the summits is a tongue of the shrinking Watson Glacier. Moats open between snow and rock by mid-to-late summer, especially in the west gully.

results.correct_value: ~2.5 mi from the trailhead to the ~4,800 ft saddle
results.evidence: The Forest Service trail page gives 1 mi to the Anderson Butte junction, another mile to the 4,700 ft second junction, then 0.5 mi up to the saddle (2.5 mi). The row's own waypoints (junctions at 1 and 2 mi, saddle at 2.5 mi) and the approach prose (second junction at 1.5-2 mi, then 0.5 mi to the saddle) agree; WTA also puts the second junction at 1.5 mi, before the saddle, so 1.4 mi to the saddle is impossible. The ~1.4 mi in the itinerary note and its timing copy is the lone outlier. Bivy text is left to the camping clean-up.

results.evidence: dist_km 84.5 km (52.5 mi) is clearly not a one-way figure. NPS/WTA-style mileages put Hayes River Guard Station at 16.1 mi from Whiskey Bend, but Camp Wilder's distance is given variously (~16 to ~20 mi) and no source states the one-way distance to the off-trail summit. An authoritative Elwha trail mileage table for Camp Wilder plus the off-trail leg would settle it.

Still no outside source for Mushroom Tower's standard-route pitch count: Mountain Project and theCrag list no routes on it, the 2010 CascadeClimbers report still does not load and has no archive copy, and a historic account describes only one hard overhanging pitch. The row itself says 2 in four fields vs 1 in beta; a readable modern trip report would settle it.

No source gives a modern grade for the tower (5.4 vs 5.5). The only historic account found describes a 12-ft overhang overcome with a shoulder stand, which fits neither figure cleanly. A readable modern trip report or guidebook entry is needed.

All sources found (Kangaroo Temple/Ridge route pages, Mazamas, WTA Kangaroo Pass report, onehikeaweek) say only 'large pullout/turnout at the hairpin turn'; one describes the start as 'tucked behind the pullout on the hairpin corner'. None states inside vs outside. A map or photo of the pullout relative to the curve would settle it.
